currentDist.help: The selected distribution: one of the continuous or discrete distributions on the left, or the attributive distribution with weighted categories. The values are regenerated at once; the parameters of every distribution stay stored, also after switching.

params.help: The parameters per continuous or discrete distribution, by distribution and parameter id, each with default and bounds; all distributions are stored, the selected one takes effect (activeParams). An agent writes the whole object with instance.set.

normal.help: The parameters of the distribution “Normal Distribution”.

mu.help: Mean (μ): the location of the distribution, around which the values scatter. Allowed: any number; default 0.

sigma.help: Std. Dev. (σ): the scale, the spread of the values around the location. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

epsilon.help: Skewness (ε): the asymmetry: 0 gives symmetric values, positive values make the distribution right-skewed (long right tail), negative values left-skewed. Allowed: any number; default 0.

delta.help: Tailweight (δ): how heavy the tails are: 1 gives the normal distribution, values below 1 make the tails heavier, values above 1 lighter. Allowed: number from 0.01; default 1.

chisquare.help: The parameters of the distribution “Chi-Square Distribution”.

k.help: Degrees of freedom (k): they set the shape of the chi-square distribution; the larger, the more symmetric. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 5.

d1.help: Degrees of freedom d₁: the number of degrees of freedom in the numerator of the F distribution. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 5.

d2.help: Degrees of freedom d₂: the number of degrees of freedom in the denominator of the F distribution. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 10.

nu.help: Degrees of freedom (ν): they set the shape of the t distribution; the larger, the closer it is to the normal distribution. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 10.

uniform.help: The parameters of the distribution “Uniform Distribution (continuous)”.

a.help: Lower bound (a): the lower bound, below which no values occur. Allowed: any number; default 0.

b.help: Upper bound (b): the upper bound, above which no values occur; it must not be less than the lower bound. Allowed: any number; default 1.

beta.help: The parameters of the distribution “Beta Distribution”.

alpha.help: Shape α: the first shape of the beta distribution; together with β it decides whether the values between 0 and 1 lie more to the left or to the right. Allowed: number from 0.01; default 2.

beta.help: Shape β: the second shape of the beta distribution; together with α it decides whether the values between 0 and 1 lie more to the left or to the right. Allowed: number from 0.01; default 5.

cauchy.help: The parameters of the distribution “Cauchy Distribution”.

x0.help: Location (x₀): the location, the center of the Cauchy distribution (its median). Allowed: any number; default 0.

gamma.help: Scale (γ): the scale, the width of the Cauchy distribution. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

exponential.help: The parameters of the distribution “Exponential Distribution”.

lambda.help: Rate (λ): the rate: how many events occur per unit; the mean of the values is 1/λ. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

gamma_dist.help: The parameters of the distribution “Gamma Distribution”.

alpha.help: Shape (α): the shape of the gamma distribution; 1 gives the exponential distribution, larger values make it more symmetric. Allowed: number from 0.01; default 2.

beta.help: Scale (β): the scale of the gamma distribution, by which all values are stretched. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

laplace.help: The parameters of the distribution “Laplace Distribution”.

mu.help: Location (μ): the location, the center of the Laplace distribution. Allowed: any number; default 0.

b.help: Scale (b): the scale, the width of the Laplace distribution. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

gumbel_max.help: The parameters of the distribution “Largest Extreme Value (Gumbel)”.

mu.help: Location (μ): the location of the Gumbel distribution for maxima (its mode). Allowed: any number; default 0.

beta.help: Scale (β): the scale, the width of the Gumbel distribution for maxima. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

logistic.help: The parameters of the distribution “Logistic Distribution”.

mu.help: Location (μ): the location, the center of the logistic distribution. Allowed: any number; default 0.

s.help: Scale (s): the scale, the width of the logistic distribution. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

loglogistic.help: The parameters of the distribution “Log-Logistic Distribution”.

alpha.help: Scale (α): the scale of the log-logistic distribution, which is also its median. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

beta.help: Shape (β): the shape of the log-logistic distribution; the larger, the more tightly the values lie around the scale. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

lognormal.help: The parameters of the distribution “Lognormal Distribution”.

mu.help: Log-Mean (μ): the mean of the logarithms of the values (not of the values themselves). Allowed: any number; default 0.

sigma.help: Log-Std.Dev. (σ): the standard deviation of the logarithms of the values (not of the values themselves). Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

gumbel_min.help: The parameters of the distribution “Smallest Extreme Value (Gumbel)”.

mu.help: Location (μ): the location of the Gumbel distribution for minima (its mode). Allowed: any number; default 0.

beta.help: Scale (β): the scale, the width of the Gumbel distribution for minima. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

triangular.help: The parameters of the distribution “Triangular Distribution”.

a.help: Minimum (a): the minimum, the smallest possible value. Allowed: any number; default 0.

c.help: Mode (c): the mode, the most frequent value; it must lie between the minimum and the maximum. Allowed: any number; default 0.5.

b.help: Maximum (b): the maximum, the largest possible value; it must not be less than the minimum. Allowed: any number; default 1.

weibull.help: The parameters of the distribution “Weibull Distribution”.

alpha.help: Shape (α): the shape of the Weibull distribution; 1 gives the exponential distribution, above 1 the failure rate rises over time. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.5.

beta.help: Scale (β): the scale of the Weibull distribution (characteristic life: 63.2 % of the values lie below it). Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

bernoulli.help: The parameters of the distribution “Bernoulli Distribution”.

p.help: Success prob. (p): the probability that a trial succeeds and yields 1; otherwise 0 results. Allowed: number from 0 to 1; default 0.5.

binomial.help: The parameters of the distribution “Binomial Distribution”.

n.help: Trials (n): how often the trial is repeated for each generated value; the value counts the successes. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 10.

p.help: Success prob. (p): the probability that a single trial succeeds. Allowed: number from 0 to 1; default 0.5.

geometric.help: The parameters of the distribution “Geometric Distribution”.

p.help: Success prob. (p): the probability that a single trial succeeds; the value counts the failures before the first success. Allowed: number from 0.0001 to 1; default 0.3.

negbinomial.help: The parameters of the distribution “Negative Binomial Distribution”.

r.help: Successes (r): how many successes are waited for; the value counts the failures up to then. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 5.

p.help: Success prob. (p): the probability that a single trial succeeds. Allowed: number from 0.0001 to 1; default 0.5.

hypergeometric.help: The parameters of the distribution “Hypergeometric Distribution”.

N.help: Population size (N): the number of all elements drawn from without replacement. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 100.

K.help: Success states (K): how many of the N elements are successes; at most as many as N. Allowed: number from 0, whole numbers are usual; default 30.

n.help: Sample size (n): how many elements are drawn for each generated value, at most as many as N; the value counts the successes among them. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 10.

a.help: Minimum (a): the smallest whole number that can occur; it should not be larger than the maximum. Allowed: any number, decimals are rounded down; default 1.

b.help: Maximum (b): the largest whole number that can occur; it should not be smaller than the minimum. Allowed: any number, decimals are rounded down; default 6.

poisson.help: The parameters of the distribution “Poisson Distribution”.

lambda.help: Rate (λ): the mean number of events per unit; it is both the mean and the variance of the values. Allowed: number from 0.01; default 5.

mvnormal.help: The parameters of the distribution “Multivariate Normal (2D)”.

mu1.help: Mean μ₁: the location of the first component of the two-dimensional normal distribution; it determines the generated values. Allowed: any number; default 0.

mu2.help: Mean μ₂: the location of the second component; the generated column holds only the first component, so μ₂ does not currently change it. Allowed: any number; default 0.

sigma1.help: Std.Dev. σ₁: the spread of the first component around its mean μ₁. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

sigma2.help: Std.Dev. σ₂: the spread of the second component around its mean μ₂; the generated column holds only the first component, so σ₂ does not currently change it. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

rho.help: Correlation ρ: how strongly the two components are related (-1 opposite, 0 independent, 1 in step); the generated column holds only the first component, so ρ does not currently change it. Allowed: number from -0.999 to 0.999; default 0.5.

count.help: Count (n): the sample size for a continuous or discrete distribution, a whole number from 1 to 100,000. A change generates the values again at once.

seed.help: Seed: the starting value of the random generator for a continuous or discrete distribution. The same seed gives the same values, so the sample is reproducible. Any whole number is allowed, 0 included; an empty field counts as 42. A change generates the values again at once.

attributes.help: The categories of the attributive distribution, each with id, name and weight; add, change and remove them with addAttribute, setAttribute and removeAttribute.

name.help: Attribute: the name of the category. It may be empty; categories without a name are skipped when generating.

weight.help: Weight of the category, a number from 0. The share of a category is its weight divided by the sum of all weights; the column "Share" shows it in percent. A category with weight 0 is skipped when generating.

attrCount.help: Count (n): the sample size for the attributive distribution, a whole number from 1 to 100,000. A change generates the values again at once.

attrSeed.help: Seed: the starting value of the random generator for the attributive distribution. The same seed gives the same values, so the sample is reproducible. Any whole number is allowed, 0 included; an empty field counts as 42. A change generates the values again at once.

generated.help: Summary of the generated values, each item described under keys; null without a selected distribution, without a valid category or when the distribution could not generate values. The values follow every change at once; the cards show the statistics with four decimals, magnitudes from 10⁶ or below 0.001 in exponential notation.

activeParams.help: The paths that take effect in the current state: params.<distribution>.<id> of the selected distribution, then count and seed; for the attributive distribution attrCount and attrSeed; empty without a selected distribution.

targetColumns.help: The targets toWorksheet accepts, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'. Per sheet with an empty column its empty columns are listed, followed by an entry with columnId '__new__' (name is the sheet name) that appends a new column. A target null creates a new worksheet.

addAttribute.help: Adds a category to the attributive distribution, with an empty name and weight 1; the values are regenerated at once. Categories without a name are skipped when generating. The agent receives the identifier of the category.

params.command: The command as an empty object; it takes no arguments.

removeAttribute.help: Removes a category of the attributive distribution; the values are regenerated at once. The last category can be removed too, then there are no values.

params.attrId: The id of a category from attributes; any other is rejected.
params.command: The command as an object with attrId.

setAttribute.help: Sets the name or weight of a category of the attributive distribution; the values are regenerated at once. Categories with an empty name or a weight of 0 are skipped when generating.

params.attrId: The id of a category from attributes or the one from addAttribute; any other is rejected.
params.key: Which field: name or weight; any other value is rejected.
params.value: The value: for name a text (empty allowed), for weight a number from 0; anything else is rejected.
params.command: The command as an object with attrId, key and value.

toWorksheet.help: Sends the generated values as a column to a new worksheet, into an existing empty column or as a new column to an existing sheet, all or nothing; a confirmation follows. Without values nothing is sent.

params.target: The target: a new worksheet, an empty column of a sheet or a new column on a sheet. Only sheets with an empty column are offered; a target that is no longer free is rejected.

cancel.help: Cancels sending as long as nothing is written yet.

Generated.n: n: the number of generated values, equal to the set count (n).
Generated.mean: Mean x̄ = Σx / n, the sum of the generated values divided by their count. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.sd: Std.Dev. s = √(Σ(x − x̄)² / (n − 1)), the sample spread of the generated values with denominator n − 1. Not defined for a single drawn value: the result is then empty. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.median: Median: the middle of the generated values sorted ascending, for an even count the mean of the two middle ones. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.min: Min: the smallest of the generated values. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.max: Max: the largest of the generated values. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.skewness: Skewness g₁ = m₃ / m₂^1.5 with the central moments m₂ = Σ(x − x̄)² / n and m₃ = Σ(x − x̄)³ / n (denominator n, not corrected). Positive: the long tail is on the right, negative: on the left; 0 for symmetric values. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.kurtosis: Kurtosis as excess: m₄ / m₂² − 3 with m₂ = Σ(x − x̄)² / n and m₄ = Σ(x − x̄)⁴ / n (denominator n, not corrected). 0 matches the normal distribution, positive means more peaked with heavy tails, negative flatter. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.frequency: The frequency per category, sorted descending by count; each entry gives name and count. The card "Categories" counts the entries, the card "Most frequent" names the first one. Only for the attributive distribution.

FrequencyRow.name: The name of the category.
FrequencyRow.count: How often the category occurs among the generated values.
FrequencyRow.share: The share of the category among all generated values, as a number from 0 to 1 (count divided by the number of values); the display shows it as a percentage.

TargetColumn.key: The target as 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'; columnId '__new__' appends a new column to the sheet.
TargetColumn.name: The name of the empty column, for the “new column” entry the name of the sheet.
